name: Okabe-Ito
summary: The eight-color palette designed so people with color blindness can tell the colors apart. Orange, sky blue, green, yellow, blue, vermillion and reddish purple, plus black.
guidance: Use the blue (primary) and orange (accent) together: they stay clearly different for every common type of color blindness.
Success (bluish green) and danger (vermillion) are the pair that stays apart best for red-green color blindness, though you should still add an icon and a label.
Built for color-blind accessibility: the hues stay distinguishable for the most common types of color blindness, mainly by differing in lightness as well as hue.
Several of these colors are too light to carry white text. Put dark text (ink) on them, as the contrast checks below show, and never white text.
Body text needs 4.5:1 against its background; large text and UI outlines need 3:1.
Still pair every status color with an icon or text. Color alone should never be the only signal.

credit.text: Masataka Okabe and Kei Ito, Color Universal Design (2008). Popularised for scientific figures by Bang Wong, Nature Methods 8, 441 (2011). The hex values are the published palette.
